problemStatement: The Weekly Radar runtime accepts configured source URLs with only a scheme-prefix check, so malformed URLs, credential-bearing URLs, local/private IP literals, and local-only host names are not rejected at configuration time. The production ureq source and Telegram agents also follow redirects by default; Telegram's endpoint embeds a bot token in the URL. This WI closes the deterministic, evidence-backed baseline while explicitly leaving DNS and full allowlist policy to a later decision.

riskAssessment.reason: The change guards external network destinations and a token-bearing Telegram endpoint. guidelines: New public APIs or changed public behavior must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.
Fail closed at the configuration/transport boundary; do not infer provider authority or research judgments.
Do not claim external provider or production behavior was verified without a real authorized receipt.
Preserve existing fixture, timeout, body-size, payload, and retry contracts unless this Contract explicitly changes them.

intent.problem: The current source configuration accepts only a URL prefix and the production HTTP agents follow redirects by default. This leaves an evidence-backed unintended-destination baseline gap at the runtime network boundary.
constraints: Reject only deterministic unsafe URL forms that can be checked without DNS or external calls.
Do not introduce a guessed provider host allowlist or alter public source authority semantics.
Disable automatic redirects for source and Telegram agents without changing their existing timeout, body-size, payload, or retry contracts.
Keep fixture transports permissive and preserve all existing public registry URLs.
Do not perform production operations or real external requests as part of this Work Item.
intent.rationale: A configuration validator plus zero-redirect transport policy closes the concrete local/private-destination and redirect risks visible in the current code while preserving the boundary for a later product-approved DNS/allowlist policy.
